rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2024, we were in compliance with all covenants under the Debt Agreements. ... Our Credit Facility is also subject to financial covenants, including the following ratios, as defined in the corresponding agreement: EBITDA to Interest Expense 2.5 to 1.0; Senior Secured Debt to EBITDA 3.0 to 1.0; Total Debt to EBITDA 5.25 to 1.0 (subject to a temporary increase to 5.50 to 1.0 for any quarter during which an acquisition satisfying certain thresholds is completed and for the two quarters immediately following such quarter).
rfm_tuples.f: going_concern_local + cross-check with Q3 2024 10-Q and Q1 2025 10-Q for any covenant amendments, waiver disclosures, or step-up in leverage ratio limits. Compute pro-forma Total Debt / EBITDA at YE24.
rfm_tuples.M_value: going_concern_local: NO_GOING_CONCERN (n_matches=0). Total debt at YE24 ~$2.2B, 2024 Adjusted Gross Margin $699M, implied Net Income + D&A + Interest + Tax run-rate puts EBITDA proxy ~$555M, giving Total Debt/EBITDA ~3.9x — well under the 5.25x covenant. rfm_tuples.interpretation: Covenant compliance is verified; no going-concern language; pro-forma leverage well below the limit; the TOPS-window step-up was disclosed and used legitimately. Strong solvency disclosure.

rfm_tuples.R: On August 30, 2024, we completed the TOPS Acquisition... for aggregate consideration consisting of $868.7 million in cash and approximately 6.9 million shares of common stock with an acquisition date fair value of $139.1 million... (preliminary purchase price allocation Q3 2024 10-Q: Property, plant and equipment $872,053; Goodwill $116,937; Intangible assets $52,775; Purchase price $1,007,723). (10-K final allocation: Property, plant and equipment $912,877; Goodwill $52,155; Intangible assets $76,228; Purchase price $1,007,723).
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution — compare Q3 2024 10-Q TOPS purchase-price allocation to 10-K final allocation; magnitude and direction of changes; whether the reallocation moves value away from goodwill (favorable for future impairment risk) or toward goodwill (concerning).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Material reallocation Q3->Final: Goodwill $116.9M -> $52.2M (-$64.8M, -55%); PP&E $872.1M -> $912.9M (+$40.8M, +4.7%); Intangibles $52.8M -> $76.2M (+$23.4M, +44%). Total consideration unchanged at $1,007.7M. The shift moves $64.8M out of goodwill and into depreciable/amortizable tangible+intangible assets. Q1 2025 10-Q reaffirms the final allocation (goodwill $52.2M stable).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The reallocation is the FAVORABLE direction for forensic purposes — moving value out of goodwill (which is impairment-tested annually as a binary cliff event) and into PP&E/intangibles (which depreciate predictably) reduces the risk of a future goodwill write-down. The magnitude (~6% of purchase price) is reasonable for a Q3->Q4 valuation refinement. No red flag.

rfm_tuples.R: During the year ended December 31, 2024, one customer accounted for $121.4 million, or more than 10% of our consolidated revenue, and another customer accounted for more than 13% of our consolidated trade accounts receivable, both primarily related to our contract operations segment. ... Our five most significant customers collectively accounted for 35%, 33% and 32% of our revenues during the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the 10% concentration is honestly framed (not hidden via segment-only basis). Mode B — derive whether the unnamed >10% customer is named anywhere (related-party note, Form 8-K, exhibit list), and whether the >13% A/R customer is the same as or different from the >10% revenue customer.
rfm_tuples.M_value: The >10% revenue customer ($121.4M = ~10.5% of $1,157.6M) is NOT named in the 10-K. Hilcorp (named in Related-Party Note 29) generated only $40.7M revenue in 2024 (3.5% of total) — so Hilcorp is NOT the >10% customer. The >13% A/R customer is also unnamed (and distinct from Hilcorp, whose A/R was only $3.6M = ~2.8% of trade A/R $123.1M). Top-5 customer concentration is stable: 35% (2024), 33% (2023), 32% (2022) — slight increase. Initial contract terms 12-36 months, then month-to-month with 30 days notice — typical for midstream services.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B partial finding — the >10% customer's identity is intentionally undisclosed (permissible under Reg S-K but reduces transparency). Top-5 concentration is moderate (35%) and stable. The fact that the >10% revenue customer and >13% A/R customer are separately disclosed (rather than combined) suggests they may be different entities, implying TWO customers at meaningful concentration. No direct red flag, but the lack of customer naming is a friction point for due diligence.

rfm_tuples.R: From August 2019 to present, our Board of Directors has included a member affiliated with our customer Hilcorp or its subsidiaries or affiliates. rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive whether related-party revenue trajectory is normal or pulled-forward, and whether the related-party A/R balance has unusual movement. Cross-check Q1 2025 10-Q for any spike in related-party transactions.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Hilcorp revenue trajectory: $36.2M (2022) -> $35.4M (2023) -> $40.7M (2024) — modest growth, no spike. BUT Hilcorp A/R jumped from $3.6M (YE24) to $14.7M (Q1 2025), of which $9.9M is 'used equipment sales' to Hilcorp in Q1 2025. Selling ~$10M of used equipment to a board-affiliated related party in a single quarter is unusual relative to the trailing 12-month revenue run-rate ($40.7M) and the prior A/R baseline ($3.6M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-06, within cutoff) reveals a $9.9M one-time related-party used-equipment sale to a Hilcorp-affiliated customer. This is fully disclosed (no fraud), but warrants attention: (i) used-equipment gains were a notable contributor to 2024 EPS ($17.6M of $17.9M total gain-on-sale), and (ii) selling materially to a board-affiliated counterparty raises arms-length-pricing questions. Not severe but a forensic yellow flag — particularly since 2024 gain-on-sale of assets was 10% of net income ($17.9M of $172.2M).

rfm_tuples.R: Implied claim — if Archrock management believed the August 2024 capital event suite (July 2024 Equity Offering $255.7M net proceeds, August 2024 6.625% Senior Notes due 2032 $700M, $202M tender of 6.875% 2027 Notes, August 30, 2024 TOPS Acquisition close $868.7M cash + 6.9M shares) was being executed at attractive prices, insiders should NOT be cluster-selling around those dates.
rfm_tuples.f: insider_vs_calendar (TEMPORAL detector) — parse all Form 4 transactions in the ±60 day window around 2024-07-24 (equity offering), 2024-08-26 (2032 Notes), and 2024-08-30 (TOPS close). Classify discretionary sales (code S) vs automatic/vesting (code F, M, A).
rfm_tuples.M_source: edgar.list_filings Form 4s + edgar.fetch_form4_xml for 2024-07-15 to 2024-10-15 window
rfm_tuples.M_value: ONLY 1 Form 4 filed in the 3-month window 2024-07-15 to 2024-10-15 (the entire capital-event corridor): a director (Honeybourne) ACQUIRED 617 shares at $20.24 via DSDP (transactionCode 'A') on 2024-09-30. Zero insider open-market sales, zero discretionary sales around the equity offering, around the bond offering, or around TOPS close. The next Form 4 cluster doesn't appear until February 2025 (vesting/withholding for 2024 LTI grants — code F, routine).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strong Mode B PASS — insiders did NOT sell into the July equity offering, did NOT monetize around the 2032 Notes, and did NOT exit at the TOPS close. The only insider transaction in the entire capital-event window was a small director DSDP acquisition. This is the OPPOSITE of the IONQ/YSS pattern — consistent with management believing the post-TOPS franchise is undervalued at the offering price range ($20-21 per share).

rfm_tuples.R: We have no near-term maturities and believe that our operating cash flows and borrowings under the Credit Facility will be sufficient to meet our future liquidity needs. ... Maturities of Long Term Debt: 2025 $0; 2026 $0; 2027 $298,542; 2028 $1,209,443; 2029 $0; Thereafter $690,391. rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify the 'no near-term maturities' claim and identify any spring-forward / acceleration provisions that could compress the maturity profile. Compute refinancing wall.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text + 10-K Note 16 Long-Term Debt + MD&A Liquidity section
rfm_tuples.M_value: Verified — no maturities in 2025 or 2026 in stated terms. BUT Credit Facility ($1.1B revolving) has SPRING-FORWARD acceleration: matures Dec 2, 2026 if any 2027 Notes are outstanding at that date, and Dec 3, 2027 if any 2028 Notes are outstanding. With $300M 2027 Notes and $1.21B 2028 Notes still outstanding, the Credit Facility effectively matures Dec 2026 unless the 2027 Notes are refinanced first. So real refinancing wall is Dec 2026 (Credit Facility), April 2027 ($300M 2027 Notes), April 2028 ($1.21B 2028 Notes). $408.3M was drawn on the Credit Facility at YE24.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — the 'no near-term maturities' summary in MD&A is technically true (no scheduled 2025 or 2026 maturities) but obscures the Dec 2026 spring-forward on the Credit Facility. The real near-term refinancing requirement is the $300M 2027 Notes by Dec 2026 to keep the Credit Facility alive. Not hidden (detail is in the Credit Facility note) but the MD&A framing is selective. Manageable given 2024 operating cash flow of $429.6M.

rfm_tuples.R: Revenue in our contract operations business increased approximately $105.6 million due to higher rates and an increase in average operating horsepower, as well as an increase of $65.5 million due to the compression units acquired in the TOPS Acquisition. ... Horsepower utilization: Spot (at period end) 96% / 96% / 93%; Average 95% / 95% / 87% (2024/2023/2022).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive whether organic growth (ex-TOPS) is real or being papered over with TOPS contribution. Compute: contract operations revenue YoY ex-TOPS = ($980.4M - $65.5M TOPS) - $809.4M = $105.5M growth on $809.4M base = ~13% organic growth. Compare to operating horsepower growth.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text + 10-K MD&A Operating Highlights + Note 30 Segments
rfm_tuples.M_value: Verified. Organic (ex-TOPS) contract operations revenue growth was ~13% ($809.4M -> ~$914.9M), driven by higher rates and higher utilization. Average operating horsepower grew from 3,554k to 3,794k (+6.8%), of which TOPS contributed an estimated ~80k average HP (530k at acquisition × 4/12 months). Adjusted gross margin % expanded from 62% to 67% — pricing power is real. Q1 2025 10-Q shows continued momentum: contract ops revenue $300.4M vs $223.1M Q1 2024 (+35%, includes full quarter of TOPS).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Organic growth is real and verifiable. Utilization at 95-96% is near-structural maximum (suggests genuine supply tightness in large-horsepower compression in the Permian/Eagle Ford). Pricing power is reflected in gross margin expansion. No evidence of TOPS being used to mask organic decline.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied claim — Archrock's disclosed organic growth and strong utilization should be MIRRORED by counterparty disclosures from upstream/midstream customers that name Archrock or its competitors as compression service providers in their own 10-Ks.

rfm_tuples.M_value: FTS returned 34 hits for 'Archrock' in 10-K filings 2024-01-01 through 2025-05-14. Inspection of top hits shows the vast majority are Archrock's own filings + their exhibits (Exhibit 21.1 subsidiaries list, Exhibit 10 contracts). The only non-AROC hit on first page is CSI Compressco LP (CCLP, CIK 0001449488) — a direct compression-services competitor — which referenced Archrock in its 10-K. No upstream/midstream counterparty filings name Archrock as a compression services provider (typical — compression contracts are usually opaque counterparty-name-wise in customer 10-Ks).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B counterparty-mirror check is largely uninformative for this industry. Compression services are infrastructure-level expenditures that customers typically don't itemize by vendor in 10-Ks. The CCLP cross-reference is a competitor mention, not a customer mention. Neither corroborates nor contradicts AROC's claims. UNVERIFIABLE rather than PASS.

Safety performance is unverifiable in absolute terms but no Item 3 disclosures contradict the safety narrative.

summary: AROC's 2024 10-K reads as an HONEST disclosure of a well-managed midstream natural gas compression franchise that completed a large transformational acquisition (TOPS, $1.0B for 580k HP from Apollo) in August 2024 funded with a clean capital stack ($255.7M equity offering + $700M new 8-year notes + $202M tender of nearer-dated notes + revolver). Deloitte issued an unqualified opinion on both financials and ICFR. No going-concern language, no material weakness, no restatement, no auditor disagreement. Pro-forma leverage ~3.9x vs 5.25x covenant. Crucially, the insider_vs_calendar Mode B check shows ZERO insider open-market sales in the entire 3-month corridor around the July equity offering, August bond offering, and TOPS close — the only Form 4 filed in that window was a small director DSDP acquisition. This is the opposite of the canonical 'capital-raise then dump' pattern. Two moderate flags: (1) Q1 2025 10-Q reveals a $9.9M used-equipment sale to board-affiliated Hilcorp in a single quarter, lifting related-party A/R from $3.6M to $14.7M — disclosed but unusual; (2) MD&A 'no near-term maturities' obscures the Credit Facility Dec 2026 spring-forward against the unrefinanced $300M 2027 Notes. The TOPS purchase-price allocation shifted favorably between Q3 2024 (preliminary $116.9M goodwill) and the 10-K (final $52.2M goodwill), reducing future impairment risk. Organic contract operations growth ~13% YoY ex-TOPS with utilization at 95% suggests genuine pricing power in large-horsepower compression. The -14.6% pre-cutoff drawdown reads as sector beta plus post-TOPS integration overhang rather than disclosed fundamental distress.
